description: Baseline capped compat workload harness; profiling points to repeated score_team work, especially personality scoring, Pydantic request construction, and compat skill assignment.
Replace statistics.pstdev-based personality scoring with a float-only one-pass implementation; removes heavy stdlib numeric overhead while preserving output on existing tests.

Add a direct scoring fast path for formation that reuses raw Person objects instead of rebuilding Pydantic TeamQualityRequest/TeamMember structures for every candidate; also cache per-member social preference maps inside team_social_score.

Thread a form_teams-level score cache through candidate generation and swap improvement so repeated task/team evaluations are reused instead of rescored; biggest win comes from improve_allocations reusing candidate scores.

Precompute shortlist-scorer invariants per task to avoid repeated task/preference/weight lookup, but the end-to-end benchmark regressed slightly; remaining cost is dominated more by candidate scoring and compat assignment than by per-person setup.

Cache per-request task lookup and filtered task preferences for score_team, but the improvement was within noise and slightly worse than the current best; static request metadata is not the main bottleneck anymore.

Cache team-only personality and social components across tasks and swap evaluations, then inject them into the direct scoring path; repeated group compositions were paying the same non-task-dependent costs many times.
Cache compat member task-value vectors by member identity and ordered task-skill ids; benchmark improved, but lint failed on a long line so the change was reverted for cleanup before retrying.
Cache compat member task-value vectors by member identity and ordered task-skill ids so repeated candidate teams stop rebuilding the same per-person skill alignment arrays for each task.

Tried a fast-path that skips compat uncovered-skill backfilling when coverage is already complete and only sorts assignments on success, but the benchmark regressed; this helper is not a worthwhile optimization target in the current workload.
Rewrote geometric_mean and weighted_geometric_mean as single-pass log accumulators to remove temporary collections, but the benchmark was slower overall; these helpers are not the next bottleneck.

Use insertion-order team ids instead of sorted ids for the cross-task personality/social cache key. The measured delta versus the current best was effectively noise-level, so this is not worth keeping as an extra behavioral assumption.

Tried collapsing several compat-assignment helper passes into one shared analysis routine, but it changed task assignment behavior on multiple formation regressions and was slower anyway; the helper interactions are more delicate than they look.

Replace compat perfect-matching recursion with a bitmask DP over positive-task masks. Behavior held on the benchmark and speed looked promising, but lint failed on formatting so the change was reverted before validation.

Replaced compat perfect-matching recursion with a bitmask DP over positive-task masks. It preserved checks but regressed the median, so the square-team feasibility check is not a profitable target on this workload.

Thread precomputed task-skill ids, order maps, and max-skills-per-member through compat uncovered-assignment cleanup to avoid rebuilding tiny structures, but the added plumbing slowed the benchmark slightly.

Tried making swap improvement compare objectives from quality lists instead of rebuilding temporary allocation lists, but the extra list churn still lost to the baseline; improve_allocations is not the main remaining bottleneck.

Tried trimming math.isclose calls inside _compat_other_member_best_values with cheaper equality fast paths, but the benchmark regressed and lint rejected the nested-condition style, so this avenue is not promising.

Added a cached task-skill metadata helper so compat scoring could reuse ordered skill ids and sort maps across repeated evaluations of the same task, but the extra cache lookups/regression overhead outweighed the tiny structure rebuilds.

Combined compat task-capability counting with other-member-best analysis so _assign_task_skills_compat can reuse one shared per-task pass; this looked like the strongest improvement so far, but ty rejected the optional counts typing and the change was reverted for a cleanup retry.

Fuse compat member-task analysis into one shared pass (member_has_match + task_capable_counts + other_member_best_values) and reuse the same task_capable_counts in member-priority ordering to remove duplicate scans of the member/task matrix.

asi.hypothesis: Combining compat matrix analyses and eliminating duplicated capable-count passes will cut _assign_task_skills_compat overhead without changing behavior.
asi.result: Slight median improvement with unchanged quality/team-count metrics.

description: Precompute per-member positive task bitmasks and per-task best values in compat analysis, then iterate only positive candidate bits during assignment and reuse precomputed best task values during uncovered rescue scoring.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask-driven candidate scanning should cut _assign_task_skills_compat inner-loop work by avoiding full task scans and repeated max() rescans.
asi.result: Large median improvement with unchanged quality/team-count metrics.

description: Attempted a fast-path to skip full uncovered-assignment rebalancing when covered_mask already spans all task skills, plus reused a per-call task_skill_order map. This changed compat assignment semantics (missing rescued skill assignments in overlap-heavy cases), so checks failed and the change was reverted.

asi.hypothesis: Bypassing _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments on full coverage should remove unnecessary assignment recounting/sorting overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Fast-path was behaviorally incorrect: it skipped expected compatibility rebalancing that preserves legacy assignment distribution invariants.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments semantics intact; target micro-optimizations inside it (fewer allocations/lookups) rather than skipping it.
asi.failure_surface: tests/test_team_quality.py compat assignment invariance and overlap-coverage checks

description: Precompute task_skill_ids once per compat assignment call and thread that tuple through member-task value caching, member-priority tie-breaking, and candidate priority generation to remove repeated task-id tuple/list reconstruction overhead.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating repeated task-skill id reconstruction in hot compat loops will reduce per-candidate overhead without behavior changes.
asi.result: Strong runtime win with stable quality/team-count metrics.

description: Threaded precomputed task_skill_ids/task_skill_order through compat uncovered-assignment sorting/filling to avoid rebuilding per-call metadata in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments, but end-to-end median regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Passing precomputed task-skill metadata into fill/sort helpers would reduce string/dict setup overhead in a hot path.
asi.rollback_reason: Added parameter plumbing and extra argument passing cost more than metadata reconstruction in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert this helper-plumbing approach; focus on reducing algorithmic work inside _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments or candidate_combinations instead.

description: Added per-task local scored-candidate memoization in build_scored_candidates/greedy_allocations to avoid repeated cached_score_team lookups, but Ruff B023 rejected closure capture of loop-scoped memo dictionaries and the attempt was reverted.

asi.hypothesis: A local memo around scored_candidate should cut redundant cache lookups for the same candidate tuples within each task loop.
asi.rollback_reason: Lint failure (B023) due loop-variable closure capture; benchmark also regressed strongly.
asi.next_action_hint: If retried, bind memo dict via default argument in closure or use functools.partial; only continue if end-to-end metric improves.

description: Tried a unique-task-skill fast path in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments that uses assigned-skill set coverage to skip full count/decrement bookkeeping when all required skills are present, but the extra set construction/regression overhead made the benchmark slower.

asi.next_action_hint: Avoid extra prechecks in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments; target lower-level loop/call overhead or different hotspots.

description: Replaced sorted team-id cache keys with request-scoped bitmask signatures for personality/social component caches to avoid per-score tuple sorting, but end-to-end runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask team signatures should be cheaper than sorting IDs for every score_team cache lookup.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra request-level bit-map lookups and bitwise accumulation outweighed tuple-sort savings on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert team-signature bitmasking; prioritize proven compat-assignment hotspots instead.

description: Reworked compat member-priority key generation to iterate precomputed positive-task bitmasks instead of full value enumeration, but the extra list/mask handling was slightly slower than the original key comprehensions.

asi.hypothesis: Using member_positive_masks in _compat_member_priority_order should reduce zero-value filtering overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Bitmask/list conversion overhead offset any gains; median regressed versus the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing priority-key comprehensions; hunt for wins outside this ordering helper.

description: Changed compat member-task value cache keys from (member_id, task_skill_ids tuple) to identity-based (id(member), id(task_skills)) with object-identity guards to avoid hashing task-skill-id tuples on every lookup, but median runtime regressed.

asi.rollback_reason: Extra identity-guard indirection and broader cache tuple payload negated lookup savings; benchmark slowed.

description: Skipped per-member sorting in _compat_sort_member_assignments when a member has 0/1 assigned skills, but this micro-optimization regressed end-to-end runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding sorted() for tiny assignment lists should trim compat assignment overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Branch/check overhead outweighed any saved sorting work on this benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add tiny conditional guards around sort; pursue coarser-grained wins.

description: Replaced shortlist reordering in candidate_combinations (dict+sort by input positions) with an input-order filter over selected shortlist IDs, but this was slower end-to-end.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding per-call position dict construction and sort should reduce shortlist overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Set construction plus full input-order scan cost more than the small sort in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing shortlist.sort path; target heavier work than shortlist ordering.

description: Replaced compat perfect-positive matching check with a member-positive-mask DFS/backtracking solver (sorted by mask sparsity) to avoid float-matrix traversal, but median runtime still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: A bitmask-only perfect-matching feasibility check should be cheaper than augmenting-path traversal over float rows.
asi.rollback_reason: Even with mask precomputation and sparse-first ordering, recursion overhead remained slower on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing matching check; focus on higher-impact hotspots like candidate scoring/selection.

description: Reduced scored shortlist expansion factor from 4 to 1 to cut candidate scoring volume; benchmark improved sharply but this violated shortlist-coverage/caching behavior guarantees and degraded specialist selection quality in regression tests.

asi.hypothesis: Lowering MAX_SCORED_COMBINATION_EXPANSION would materially reduce candidate_combinations work in capped search.
asi.rollback_reason: Behavior changed too much: shortlist expansion tests, cache reuse expectations, and capped specialist-quality regressions failed.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting candidate caps, preserve tested expansion semantics (or update tests with a principled algorithm change) rather than tuning the global constant blindly.
asi.failure_surface: tests/test_form_teams.py scored-cap shortlist and specialist-preservation cases

description: Refactored candidate_combinations heap ranking loop to compare score/tie-break scalars before constructing replacement tuples, aiming to reduce per-combination tuple churn, but this regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding full entry-tuple construction on non-competitive combinations should speed scored shortlist ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra Python-level branching/indexing cost outweighed tuple-allocation savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original tuple-comparison heap loop; focus on larger-grain reductions in scored candidate volume or scoring cost.

description: Add a fast path in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments for max_skills_per_member==1 (the common equal-team-size compat case): directly fill uncovered skills into empty members and return without the generic rebalance/sort passes.

asi.hypothesis: When each member can hold at most one task skill, the generic uncovered rebalance loops and final sort are unnecessary overhead.
asi.result: Meaningful median improvement with unchanged quality metrics and passing checks.

description: Tried broadening the uncovered-assignment fast-path guard to `len(task_skills) <= len(assignments)` (instead of using computed max_skills_per_member==1), but this variant regressed despite equivalent behavior/checks.

asi.hypothesis: Checking len(task_skills)<=len(assignments) directly would be a cheaper trigger for the one-skill-per-member fast path.
asi.rollback_reason: This guard/flow shape was slower in practice (likely branch/layout effects) versus the prior explicit max_skills_per_member path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the previous max_skills_per_member==1 fast-path implementation from the kept commit.

description: Attempted to fold compat member-priority tuple precomputation into _compat_member_task_analysis (returning prebuilt scarce/rich priority tuples) and simplify _compat_member_priority_order to index sorting, but this added too much work to the analysis pass and regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Precomputing priority tuples during existing analysis loops would remove repeated member/task scans in _compat_member_priority_order.
asi.rollback_reason: The expanded analysis phase and extra tuple/list allocations outweighed saved scans.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep priority computation separate; avoid heavy tuple materialization in _compat_member_task_analysis.

description: Switch score_cache keys from string-id tuples to object-identity tuples (`tuple(id(person) for person in people)`) to cut hot-path key construction overhead in cached_score_team while keeping per-form-request cache scope unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: Identity-based candidate keys are cheaper to build than repeatedly reading person.id strings for every cached_score_team lookup.
asi.result: Clear median/best improvement with unchanged quality metrics and passing checks.

description: Changed greedy tie-break key to use candidate.people insertion order instead of sorting member IDs per candidate (to reduce per-candidate sorting overhead), but runtime regressed slightly.

asi.hypothesis: Dropping sorted(member.id) in greedy tie-break should save repeated tiny sorts during best-candidate selection.
asi.rollback_reason: The alternate tie-break shape was slightly slower overall and not worth behavioral risk.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing sorted-ID tie-break; focus on larger hotspots.

description: Added a fixed-size (len==4) fast path for cached_score_team key construction to avoid generator/tuple-building overhead on the benchmark’s common team size, but median result was effectively unchanged and slightly worse.

asi.hypothesis: Manual tuple construction for 4-person teams should shave overhead from the hottest cache-key path.
asi.rollback_reason: No consistent improvement over the current best; likely within noise/branch overhead.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep generic identity-tuple key path unless a broader small-team specialization proves faster.

description: Make score_cache keys order-insensitive by sorting person object identities (`tuple(sorted(id(person) ...))`) so equivalent teams in different member orders reuse cached score_team results.

asi.hypothesis: Many cached_score_team calls revisit the same team composition in different order; canonicalized keys should increase cache-hit rate enough to offset tiny sort cost.

asi.result: Large improvement with unchanged quality metrics and passing checks.

description: Tried replacing `tuple(sorted(...))` canonical key construction with list-build + in-place `.sort()` in cached_score_team, but this was slower despite equivalent semantics.

asi.hypothesis: List+sort might be a cheaper canonicalization path than sorted(generator) for order-insensitive score-cache keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra list allocation/mutation overhead outweighed any generator savings; median regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the tuple(sorted(...)) canonicalization that produced the large cache-hit win.

description: Changed request-level personality/social cache signatures from sorted member ID strings to sorted member object identities, aiming to avoid string-property work in score_team, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Identity-based team signatures should be cheaper than sorting member.id strings for component-cache keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Cache-key identity canonicalization here underperformed; likely due reduced locality/lookup characteristics versus string IDs.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep string-id team signatures for personality/social caches while retaining order-insensitive identity keys for score_cache.

description: Tried conditional canonicalization of score-cache member identity tuples (only sort when IDs are out of order) to avoid unnecessary sorts, but lint rejected zip() without strict= and benchmark performance regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Most candidate tuples are already monotonic by object id, so sorting only on inversions should preserve cache hits while reducing sort overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Implementation hit Ruff B905 (missing strict=) and showed no runtime benefit anyway.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon conditional-sort variant; keep unconditional tuple(sorted(...)) canonicalization from the kept change.

description: Added dual score-cache lookup (ordered identity key first, canonical sorted key second) and backfilled aliases to avoid sorting on exact-order repeats, but this increased cache bookkeeping overhead and regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Two-tier ordered→canonical cache keys would cut repeated canonical-sort work while preserving order-insensitive reuse.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra dictionary operations/alias writes outweighed saved sorting in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep single canonical key lookup path (sorted identities) for score_cache.

description: Removed sorted() from score_team’s personality/social cache team signature (using tuple(member.id) insertion order instead), but poorer cross-task cache reuse outweighed the saved sort cost and runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: With order-insensitive score_cache keys, score_team could avoid sorting member IDs for component-cache keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Order-sensitive signatures reduced component-cache hit rate enough to outweigh sort savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sorted member-id signatures for personality/social caches.

description: Tried replacing score_cache task key from task_id string to id(task_id) integer identity in cached_score_team, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Integer task identity keys might hash/compare faster than task_id strings in hot score_cache lookups.
asi.rollback_reason: No speedup observed; identity-key variant performed worse.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep string task_id component in score_cache keys.

description: Specialized _assign_task_skills_compat member assignment loop for max_skills_per_member==1 to bypass per-member inner-loop scaffolding, but the duplicated branch path increased overhead and regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: A dedicated single-assignment path in _assign_task_skills_compat should reduce inner-loop overhead in the common square-team workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branch duplication and code-path overhead outweighed loop simplification.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep generic member assignment loop; the fill-stage fast path is the profitable specialization.

description: Replaced sorted identity-tuple score_cache keys with request-scoped team bitmask keys (order-insensitive int masks via cached person-id->bit map), but map lookups/bit assembly regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask team keys should avoid per-call identity sorting while keeping order-insensitive score-cache hits.
asi.rollback_reason: Per-call person_id map lookups and mask accumulation were slower than tuple(sorted(id(...))) in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain sorted-identity tuple keys for score_cache; bitmasking is not a win here.

description: Inlined individual_fit logic into shortlist_scorers with precomputed task/similarity/preference invariants to avoid repeated per-person lookups, but this increased per-scorer work/allocation overhead and regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Precomputing shortlist invariants once should reduce candidate scoring overhead inside scorer().
asi.rollback_reason: The inlined path added enough Python-level list/sort work that it underperformed the existing function-based path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current shortlist scorer implementation; avoid large scorer rewrites unless supported by fresh profiling evidence.

description: Added optional precomputed task/similarity/preferences/weights inputs to individual_fit and wired shortlist_scorers to pass them, but the broader call signature/plumbing overhead regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing shortlist-level invariants in individual_fit would reduce repeated lookup/resolve work during candidate ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra argument plumbing and branching inside individual_fit offset the intended savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler individual_fit call path; avoid adding many optional precompute branches there.

description: Added an early set-based uncovered-skill fast path in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments for the one-skill-per-member regime (unique task skill IDs + <=1 assignment per member), but extra guards/set work regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: When each member has at most one assignment, uncovered detection can use set membership instead of count/decrement bookkeeping.
asi.rollback_reason: Guard checks and set construction overhead outweighed savings from simplified uncovered detection.
asi.next_action_hint: Stick with the existing max_skills_per_member==1 fast path; avoid additional precheck-heavy branches.

asi.hypothesis: candidate_combinations returns the same tuple objects later consumed by callers, so id(candidate)-keyed local memoization should skip duplicate cache lookups cheaply.
asi.rollback_reason: Local memo bookkeeping overhead outweighed saved lookups in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add extra per-task memo layers on top of score_cache here.

description: Replaced math.isclose checks with direct float equality in _compat_member_task_analysis (best/second-best tracking and unique-best detection), but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Direct equality comparisons on cached compat skill levels should be cheaper than repeated math.isclose calls in hot analysis loops.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite cheaper comparisons, this rewrite slowed end-to-end performance in the benchmark.

asi.hypothesis: Using map(id, people) might reduce generator overhead in canonical score-cache key construction.
asi.rollback_reason: No benefit observed; this variant regressed relative to the current best.

description: Precomputed explicit social-preference neighbor sets in shortlist_scorers and threaded them into candidate_social_potential to avoid repeated has_explicit_social_preferences scans, but added set/dict overhead regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing repeated preference-list scans with prebuilt neighbor sets would speed candidate_social_potential in compat mode.
asi.rollback_reason: Set materialization/lookups and extra branching were slower than the current path on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing social-potential checks; this precompute strategy is not profitable here.

description: Added request-scoped cache of canonical people-key tuples keyed by tuple-object identity to avoid repeated `tuple(sorted(id(...)))` work in cached_score_team, but cache lookup/identity-guard overhead regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing canonicalized score-cache people keys for repeated candidate tuple objects should cut sort overhead in cached_score_team.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra dictionary and identity-guard bookkeeping outweighed saved key canonicalization cost.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct canonicalization path in cached_score_team; focus on larger hotspots such as _compat_member_priority_order or candidate_combinations.

description: Tried reducing tuple materialization in _compat_member_priority_order by keeping priority lists as sorted lists (and switching rich path to generator-based sorted input), but this regressed runtime significantly.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding tuple(...) wrapping in member-priority keys should cut allocation overhead in a hot compat helper.

description: Replaced full ranking sorts in candidate_combinations with `heapq.nlargest(shortlist_size, ...)` for primary and alternate scorers to avoid sorting entire people lists, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Since shortlist extraction only consumes top shortlist_size entries, nlargest should be cheaper than full sorted(..., reverse=True).
asi.rollback_reason: For this workload (small people lists, many invocations), nlargest overhead outweighed full-sort costs.

description: In _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments, moved max_skills_per_member computation earlier and skipped _compat_sort_member_assignments when no uncovered skills and max_skills_per_member==1 (single-skill lists already ordered), but median runtime still regressed.

asi.rollback_reason: frozenset creation/hash overhead outweighed saved sort work in this benchmark.

description: Attempted to cut _compat_member_task_analysis second-pass comparisons by precomputing each task's unique best member index and building other_member_best_values from copied best-values rows with targeted overrides, but lint failed (SIM108) and runtime trend was slower anyway.

description: Tested order-insensitive score_cache keys based on sorted person.id strings (instead of sorted object identities) to avoid id() calls, but this remained slower than the current best identity-based canonical key.

asi.hypothesis: String-id canonicalization might outperform id()-based key construction while preserving order-insensitive cache hits.

description: Added local method bindings (`seen_ids.__contains__`, `seen_ids.add`) and person_id local extraction in candidate_combinations shortlist dedup loop to reduce repeated attribute lookups, but this regressed.

description: Implemented a fixed-size 4-item integer sorting network in cached_score_team for the dominant team-size case to avoid generic sorted() during score-cache key canonicalization, but this regressed.

description: Added early-return fast path in `_assign_task_skills_compat` for square teams when greedy matching already covers every task with positive assignments (`len(task_skills)==len(team)==len(matched_values)`), skipping uncovered/rescue/perfect-matching checks. This regressed.

description: Adjusted `_compat_member_priority_order` rich-first key construction to sort a generator instead of first materializing a list comprehension, aiming to trim temporary list allocation overhead. This regressed.

description: Optimized `_compat_has_perfect_positive_matching` to reuse a tokenized `seen_tasks` array instead of allocating a fresh boolean list for each augmenting-path attempt. End-to-end benchmark regressed.

description: Conditioned expensive `_compat_has_perfect_positive_matching` call on `rescued_values` being non-empty in square-team compat path (skip matching check when greedy already positively covered every task). Runtime improved versus other recent attempts but still did not beat current best.

asi.hypothesis: If no rescue values are needed, greedy already established a positive one-to-one cover in square teams, so perfect-matching verification is redundant.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite being faster than many alternatives, end-to-end median remained above incumbent best commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep as a possible revisit only if combined with a larger compat-path change that further reduces assignment overhead.

description: Bound `math.isclose` to a local `isclose` inside `_compat_member_task_analysis` and switched hot comparisons to that local reference to reduce repeated global attribute lookups. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Local-binding `math.isclose` should trim overhead in the hottest compat-analysis comparisons.
asi.rollback_reason: Lookup savings were negligible and did not offset added local plumbing in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct `math.isclose` calls in `_compat_member_task_analysis`.

description: Replaced string task-skill tie-break fields with precomputed integer lexical ranks in compat member-priority and candidate-priority tuples (`task_skill_sort_keys`) to reduce string comparisons, but this regressed.

asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct `task_skill_ids` string tie-break fields unless sort-key preprocessing can be amortized across many calls.

description: Introduced an uncapped-greedy shortcut in `greedy_allocations`: when `C(remaining_people, team_size) <= max_candidate_teams`, skip `shortlist_scorers` and pass a zero scorer (unused by candidate_combinations early-return branch). This regressed substantially.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding shortlist scorer construction for tasks that already enumerate all combinations should remove unnecessary per-task potential calculations.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branch/combination counting plus altered control flow produced worse overall runtime despite seeming to skip work.

description: Rewrote `_compat_member_task_analysis` outer scan to iterate task columns via `enumerate(zip(*member_task_values))` instead of per-member indexing (`task_values[task_index]`), aiming to reduce indexing overhead. This regressed and failed Ruff B905 (`zip` strictness requirement).

description: In `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments`, moved `max_skills_per_member` earlier and added no-uncovered fast path that returns assignments directly when `max_skills_per_member==1` (avoiding `_compat_sort_member_assignments` on single-item lists). This regressed.

asi.rollback_reason: Added branch/reordered flow did not improve performance and slowed benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing no-uncovered path with `_compat_sort_member_assignments`; this singleton shortcut is not worthwhile.

description: Refactored compat analysis to also compute per-member positive task-index lists and reused them in `_compat_member_priority_order` to avoid re-scanning full member task vectors. Initial attempt failed type checking due outdated empty-return arity.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing precomputed positive task indices should reduce repeated scan work in compat priority ordering.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra list/tuple construction in analysis outweighed savings from reduced scan conditions.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add positive-index list materialization in this path; look for reductions that avoid new per-call allocations.

description: Added an early-return in `_compat_sort_member_assignments` that skips task-order sorting when every member has 0/1 assigned skills (sorting would be a no-op). End-to-end runtime still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Many compat assignments are singleton per member, so bypassing redundant sorted() calls should cut `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` overhead.

description: Threaded precomputed `uncovered_skill_ids` from `_assign_task_skills_compat` into `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` to avoid rebuilding assigned-count/uncovered-scan state in every return path. This regressed.

description: Precomputed per-person explicit teammate-id sets once in shortlist_scorers and used set membership in candidate_social_potential (instead of repeated has_explicit_social_preferences scans) for COMPAT social gating. This regressed.

description: Tried a greedy-selection redesign: when candidate_combinations already used scored ranking (`total_candidates > max_candidate_teams`), evaluate candidates only until quality drops below the top score and apply deterministic tie-break only within that top-quality prefix. asi.rollback_reason: Extra branching/boolean logic increased overhead more than it reduced `math.isclose` usage.

description: Refactored `improve_allocations` trial evaluation to compute objective deltas from cached quality aggregates (product/min/sum) instead of rebuilding `trial_allocations` and re-running `allocation_objective` on each attempted swap/replacement. asi.rollback_reason: Despite a sizable speedup versus recent variants, median runtime still did not beat the existing best kept commit.

description: Combined three previously promising reductions: (1) `_task_preference_score` direct fast path/log loop, (2) gate square-team `_compat_has_perfect_positive_matching` behind non-empty `rescued_values`, and (3) objective-delta trial evaluation in `improve_allocations` to avoid per-trial allocation copies/objective recomputation. asi.hypothesis: These near-win changes target independent hotspots (_task_preference_score, compat perfect-matching checks, and swap objective evaluation) and should stack to exceed any single-change gain.

asi.rollback_reason: Despite strong relative improvement, median still did not beat best kept commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider combining this lazy-other-member-best approach with another independent compat-path reduction.

description: Combined four independent hotspot reductions into one patchset: (1) `_task_preference_score` direct fast path/log loop (avoids geometric_mean generator/list overhead), (2) square-team compat perfect-matching check gated behind non-empty `rescued_values`, (3) `_compat_member_task_analysis` no longer materializes `other_member_best_values` matrix (lazy per-candidate computation in `_assign_task_skills_compat`), and (4) `improve_allocations` uses objective-delta math instead of per-trial list-copy+allocation_objective recomputation. This produced a clear new best while preserving quality metrics/checks.

asi.hypothesis: Stacking several near-win, behavior-preserving reductions across independent hot paths should compound into a true end-to-end win.

description: Inlined singleton explicit-social checks directly inside `candidate_social_potential` (removed set construction and `has_explicit_social_preferences` helper calls for COMPAT pair gating). This regressed versus new best.

asi.next_action_hint: Keep current helper-based social gating.

This regressed vs current best.

description: Optimized the new objective-delta `improve_allocations` path by precomputing per-round helper data (`clamped_qualities`, `min_without_index`, and per-pair `other_min`) so inner swap/replacement loops avoid repeated per-trial scans and repeated `max(..., 1e-12)` work. description: Special-cased `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` for `max_skills_per_member==1` earlier in the flow: compute `max_skills_per_member` up front and return assignments directly when no uncovered skills (skipping `_compat_sort_member_assignments`), while preserving duplicate-skill count handling.
